Adds rapid hits of the same type on the same target into one number. Critical hits, healing and fire stay separate from ordinary hits. Adjust Combine hits within to set the timing. Ready-made looks may enable this; turn it off here to show separate hits.

Combines matching hits on one target during this window after the first hit. 250 milliseconds is a quarter of a second. Higher values allow more time to add hits to the total. Requires Combine rapid hits.
Place this world bar above the head or near the feet. A screen-pinned player bar uses its selected screen anchor.
Off hides this type; When hurt shows it below full health or condition; Always keeps it visible. Server limits still apply.
The number beside an animal's bar, on a switch of its own, so a farm can stay plain while the zombies carry one.
Base height multiplier inherited by every health and condition bar.
Maximum bars per target type. Lower this to reduce crowded overlays.
Place this world bar above the head or near the feet. A screen-pinned player bar uses its selected screen anchor.
Bar visibility range as a percentage of the normal reach. Camera zoom and the server range cap also apply.
Base width multiplier inherited by every health and condition bar.
Turn this off to hide every zombie, animal, vehicle and player bar. The settings below do not change, so turning this back on restores the same setup. A server can turn this off for everyone.
The star behind that word. Requires Show BOOM!! When An Explosion Hits Nothing. Turn it off to keep the word on its own.

The same word and star with no number under it, on the tile the blast went off on. It is drawn only when the blast damaged nothing at all, because when it did the numbers already say where it was. It is there so a bomb that misses still tells you where it landed. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Opens a gallery of every ready-made look in every colour palette. Click a card to load it, then Apply to keep it.
Copies the code above to the clipboard. Anyone with this mod can paste it to get the same settings on this page.
The colour of the star behind a critical hit. It is a setting of its own, so the star can sit under the number instead of matching it.
The star that opens behind the number. Requires Show Critical Hit Number, Star And Banner. It is the loudest part of the effect. Turn it off to keep the pale gold number and the word without it.
Changes both the critical hit number and the word CRITICAL!!. The star behind them has its own colour setting below.

A critical hit is a strong hit the game gives you at random. It gets a bigger number in pale gold, a star, and CRITICAL!! above. Melee only: a gun turns its critical hits into headshots. This is the main switch for the critical hit settings below. A server can turn this off for everyone.
The word above the number. Requires Show Critical Hit Number, Star And Banner. Turn it off to keep the bigger pale gold number and the star. The number then flies the path any other number takes.

Shows the ordinary white number over a character or animal you hit. Critical hits, headshots, instant kills and explosion damage are special versions of this number, so this switch controls them too. Other number sections and health bars remain available. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Turn off Show bars on targets in the dark to use this setting.
Set Own bar anchor to Over Your Character to use this setting.
Enable vehicle damage numbers or vehicle health bars to use this setting. The world rules must allow the feature.
The world rules do not allow: %1. Your preference is kept.
Includes damage you take from fire, falls and vehicle collisions. Requires Show damage taken. Bleeding, infection, hunger and thirst are not shown. World rules still apply.

Turns on the master switch, puts every bar on Always and shows every optional bar detail. Range, limits, size, position, colours and unseen-target visibility stay unchanged. Server limits still apply. Click Apply to save, or Cancel to undo.

Turns on the master switch and every number, banner, burst and hit marker in this section. Font, size, timing, motion, aggregation and colours stay unchanged. Server limits still apply. Click Apply to save, or Cancel to undo.
The colour of the star behind it. It starts a hot orange.
The star behind the number. Requires Show Explosion Number, Star And BOOM!!. Turn it off to keep the bigger number and the word without it.
The colour of the number and of the word over it. It starts a pale amber, hot but light enough to read over fire and smoke.

Damage from anything that explodes is drawn the way a critical hit is: a bigger number, a star, and BOOM!! over the top. One lands on each thing the blast caught. Turn it off and that damage goes back to an ordinary white number. This is the main switch for the explosion settings below. A server can turn this off for everyone.

The word above the number. Requires Show Explosion Number, Star And BOOM!!. Turn it off to keep the bigger number and the star. A bomb in a crowd is one of these on every zombie it caught, so this is the one to reach for if that is a lot.
Colour of damage numbers on burning zombies. Requires Show burning-zombie damage.
Seconds between damage numbers on burning zombies.
Page %1 of %2. Click a card to load that look, then click Apply in the settings to keep it.

A broken window is drawn in this colour instead. It starts a strong cyan, because a window going in is the easiest car damage to miss. It is deeper than the pale blue a door or a headshot uses, so the three do not blur.
The colour of the star behind a headshot. It is a setting of its own, so the star can sit under the number instead of matching it.
The star that opens behind the number. Requires Show Headshot Number, Star And Banner. It is the loudest part of the effect. Turn it off to keep the light blue number and the word without it.
Changes both the headshot number and the word HEADSHOT!!. The star behind them has its own colour setting below.

A bullet in a zombie's head gets a bigger light blue number, a star, and HEADSHOT!! above. The game makes that damage 3 times larger, so it usually kills. This is the main switch for the headshot settings below. A server can turn this off for everyone.
The word above the number. Requires Show Headshot Number, Star And Banner. Turn it off to keep the bigger light blue number and the star.
The colour of the heart behind a healing number. You need Show The Healing Heart to see it at all.
A heart that opens behind the number. This starts off. Healing comes slowly over time rather than in one moment, so there is no moment to mark.
Changes the number that shows health returning. The optional heart behind it has its own colour setting below.
Health coming back, as a green number beside you. Healing is slow, so the mod adds it up and shows one number instead of many small ones. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Off hides this type; When hurt shows it below full health or condition; Always keeps it visible. Server limits still apply.
The colour of a bar at full health. As health falls to half, the bar blends from this colour into the half-health colour.
The colour of a bar at exactly half health. Above it the bar blends up to the full-health colour, below it down to the no-health colour.
The colour of a bar as it empties. From half health down to zero the bar blends from the half-health colour into this one.
The number beside a zombie's bar, counting down from 100 to 0, in the same font as the damage numbers. A server can turn this off for everyone.
%1 settings are hidden because your choices or the world rules switch them off.

Recent health loss shows damage just taken. Toughness adds a zombie strength strip. Percentages show health remaining. NPC frame colours distinguish friends from enemies when using an NPC mod. Bar colours set the gradient every bar drains through.
Set world bar positions, then shared sizes. 100 means normal size; 150 means 50 percent larger. Vehicle sizes multiply the shared sizes. Use Own health bar for your screen anchor and personal size.
Choose which targets get bars and when. Lower range or the count limit to reduce clutter. Inspection temporarily reveals a bar; unseen-target bars need world permission.
Choose damage dealt, the ranged hit marker and missed-swing feedback. The hit marker can stay on while damage dealt numbers are hidden.
Choose object and vehicle damage. Vehicle scan range and count also affect vehicle bars.
Choose burning-zombie damage and explosion effects. A longer fire interval shows fewer popups. Explosion hits and blasts without a target have separate switches.
Adjust feedback about your character below: damage taken, wounds, healing and skill gains. Each group has its own switch and colours.
Start here. Choose a ready-made look and load it, or roll a random one. Everything and Basics change feature switches only. Open a section below to fine-tune.
Save replaces a slot immediately; Load stays pending until Apply. A settings code carries this page to another player.
For each hit type, enable its effects first. A banner is the text above the number; a burst is the decoration behind it. Use the colour controls to change each part.

Start with font and size. Increase display time to read numbers longer, or lower opacity to make them more transparent. Reduce motion keeps popups still; Combine rapid hits adds repeated hits on one target into a total. Hover a control for details.
Choose when your bar appears, then pin it over your character or to a screen edge. Width, height, segments and readouts are separate from other bars.
The colour of that number. You see this one most, so it starts white, which reads over any ground.

Shows a brief cross at the cursor when a bullet hits. It uses the headshot burst colour for headshots. Requires Enable numbers and effects, but works even when Show damage dealt is off. World rules still apply.
The colour of that number. Fire, falls and cars use it too.
Hold the right mouse button and point at a zombie to see its bar, even one nobody has hit yet. A server can turn this off for everyone.
The colour of the star behind an instant kill. It is a setting of its own, so the star can sit under the number instead of matching it.
The star that opens behind the number. Requires Show Instant Kill Number, Star And Banner. It is the loudest part of the effect. Turn it off to keep the number and the word without it.
Changes both the instant kill number and the word INSTAKILL!!. The star behind them has its own colour setting below.

A knife pushed into a zombie's jaw kills it at once. That kill gets a bigger number in bone white, a star, and INSTAKILL!! above. When one hit is both, you see this instead of a critical hit. This is the main switch for the instant kill settings below. A server can turn this off for everyone.
The word above the number. Requires Show Instant Kill Number, Star And Banner. Turn it off to keep the bigger bone white number and the star.
The colour of the wings behind the words. It is a setting of its own, so they can sit under the words instead of matching them.

The pair of wings that opens behind the words. Turn them off to keep the words on their own. The four hits that land use a star. This one uses wings, healing uses a heart, and a missed swing uses a puff of air.
The colour of the words LEVEL UP!!. They have no number under them, so this is their whole colour.
The words LEVEL UP!! appear over you when one of your skills reaches a new level. It does not say which skill. A server can turn this off for everyone.
How much light has to reach a target before it gets a bar, once bars in the dark are off. Higher asks for more light. Daylight counts outdoors, and so does a torch you are carrying.
Stages this slot for this mod page. Click Apply to save the loaded settings, or Cancel to undo the load.
Preset description: Bars on hurt zombies, animals and your own character, with recent damage and toughness detail.
Preset description: Smaller continuous bars with recent-damage feedback and no toughness strip.
Preset description: A plain, small zombie bar after damage. Keeps right-click inspection; other bars are off.
Preset description: Wider, thicker bars with percentages for zombies, animals and your own health.
Preset description: Five divisions and percentage labels. Includes damaged vehicles and your own health.
Preset description: Large Bungee numbers with colourful banners and bursts for special hits.
Preset description: Classic pixel numbers with clear special-hit labels and fewer decorative bursts.
Preset description: Cinzel lettering with warm gold damage and soft mint healing.
Preset description: Small clean numbers, reduced motion and combined rapid hits. Shows dealt and taken damage only.
Preset description: Large rounded Fredoka numbers, longer display time and fewer decorative bursts.
Choose a preset to read its description. Choosing alone does not change settings or the preview. Click Load preset to try it, then Apply to save.

Shows recent health loss on zombie and animal bars, and recent condition loss on vehicle bars, as a white strip. The strip pauses briefly, then drains down to the current value. Your own bar has a separate switch below.

Turns on the master switch and keeps a plain bar on hurt zombies plus right click inspection. Other bars and optional details turn off. Range, limits, size, position, colours and unseen-target visibility stay unchanged. Click Apply to save, or Cancel to undo.

Turns on the master switch and keeps only damage you deal and damage you take, including fire, falls and collisions. Other effects turn off. Font, size, timing, motion, aggregation and colours stay unchanged. Click Apply to save, or Cancel to undo.
The colour of the puff around the word MISS. You need Show The Miss Puff to see it at all.
A ring of sharp air streaks opens around the word, like the swing cut straight past its target. This starts off: a missed swing is the one thing worth the least noise.
The colour of the word MISS. It has no number under it, so this is its whole colour.
When you swing a melee weapon and hit nothing, the white word MISS lands where you stand. It only appears when a zombie was close enough to be your target. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Place this world bar above the head or near the feet. A screen-pinned player bar uses its selected screen anchor.
The frame around an NPC's bar when that NPC is hostile to you. It starts a dark red, deep enough that the health inside it still reads.
The same frame on an NPC who is not hostile. It starts a dark blue, the furthest thing from the red without lighting the frame up.

With an NPC mod installed, the frame around the bar turns dark red on a character that will attack you and dark blue on one that will not. The bar itself still shows health the same way. With no NPC mod this does nothing.

Turn this off to hide every damage number, banner, burst and hit marker. The settings below do not change, so turning this back on restores the same setup. Health bars are controlled separately. A server can turn this off for everyone.
The colour of that number. It starts a pale steel blue, so a door reads apart from the white over a zombie at a glance.

A number when you hit a door, a window, a barricade, furniture or a tree. It is the health your swing took off. A door is counted on a scale of its own, so it does not read like the number over a zombie and the displayed multiplier leaves it alone. It starts off, because breaking into a house is a lot of swings. On a multiplayer client it stays quiet, because the server settles a door and never says by how much. A server can turn this off for everyone.
A coordinated set of colours for this page. Choosing one changes colours only: sizes, limits and motion settings are kept.
Additional height multiplier for your bar, on top of the shared base height.
Place this world bar above the head or near the feet. A screen-pinned player bar uses its selected screen anchor.
Follow your character or pin your own bar to a screen edge inside your viewport.
Additional width multiplier for your bar, on top of the shared base width.
Off hides this type; When hurt shows it below full health or condition; Always keeps it visible. Server limits still apply.
The number beside your own bar, counting down from 100. It is body health, the number the health panel shows, and it has a switch of its own so a zombie's bar can stay plain.
The white strip on your own bar, the same as the one on a zombie's, on a switch of its own.
Number of divisions on your own bar. Zero gives a continuous bar.
How long numbers and banners stay visible. 100 uses the original timing; 200 lasts twice as long; 50 lasts half as long. Increase this if numbers disappear before you can read them.
Opacity of numbers, banners and decorative bursts. Lower values are more transparent.
Enable this bar in settings to preview it.
Samples run from healthy to nearly empty so every bar colour shows. White shows recent damage; blue shows zombie toughness. Samples are enlarged up to 2x. Game size follows settings and zoom.
Open or close a draggable preview of zombie, animal, vehicle and player bars. It updates from unsaved settings while you adjust them. Select Apply to save the changes.
Preview of your current edits. Apply saves them; Cancel restores saved settings.
Click an effect to replay it, or choose Auto to cycle. Dimmed effects are disabled by your settings or world rules.
Open or close a draggable preview of your numbers and banners. It updates from unsaved settings while you adjust them. Select Apply to save the changes.
Scroll inside this window to see more.
Tries a different coordinated palette. Keeps the shape, size and motion you have set. Apply saves it; Cancel undoes it.
Tries a ready-made look with a fresh palette and a size that is visibly different from the last one. Apply saves it; Cancel undoes it.
Keeps numbers and banners in place while they fade. Removes bouncing, drifting, growth and burst animation. Ready-made looks may enable this; turn it off here if you want motion again.
Restores every Pixel Health Bars setting to its original value. Pixel Strike Indicator settings do not change. Click Apply to save, or Cancel to undo.
Restores every Pixel Strike Indicator setting to its original value. Pixel Health Bars settings do not change. Click Apply to save, or Cancel to undo.
Restores saved settings on this page. The other page, other mods and personal slots are kept.
Immediately saves pending settings for this mod page, replacing the selected slot. Cancel does not undo a slot save.
Multiplier for displayed damage only: 100 shows 1.5 as 150. It does not change damage dealt. The server can cap it.
No matching settings. Try a shorter name, or clear the search.
%1 matching settings. Clear the search to return to your section.
Show bars on targets in the dark

Allows bars on zombies, animals, vehicles and NPCs standing in darkness. Starts off, so a bar waits until light reaches its target and an unlit room and an unlit night keep whatever is in them to themselves. Turn it on for a bar whatever the light. A server can turn this off for everyone.

Allows bars on unseen zombies, animals, vehicles and NPCs, including targets behind walls or in dark rooms. Starts off, so world bars normally appear only while your character can see their target. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Number of divisions on world bars. Zero gives a continuous bar.
The red number beside you when something hurts you. It flies to the left, and the damage you deal flies to the right, so the two never look the same. A server can turn this off for everyone.
Type part of a setting name to search every section on this page. Clear the text or choose a section to return. Searching keeps your pending edits.
Choose a section. Switching sections keeps pending edits. Type to find a section.
Clipboard unavailable. Select the code above and copy it yourself.
This page's settings as one code. Paste somebody else's here, then select «Use settings code».
Settings code copied. Paste it anywhere to share this page.
That code is incomplete or mistyped. Ask for a fresh copy.
No code found. Paste one into the box, then click again.
That is not a settings code. Copy the whole code, including PSI1.
Settings code loaded. Click «Apply» to keep it.
That code needs a newer version of this mod.
That code belongs to the other settings page. Open that page and paste it there.
Show settings that do not apply
Sections list only the settings your choices and the world rules allow. Tick this to list every setting, with the unavailable ones dimmed. Searching finds them either way.
Size of numbers and banners. 100 is the original size; 150 is 50 percent larger; 50 is half size. Open the number preview to compare.
Loaded slot %1. Click Apply to use it.
Could not load slot %1. It may be damaged or belong to another page. Your settings were kept.
Could not verify the save to slot %1. Try another slot.
Three separate slots for numbers and health bars. Slots are stored locally.
Pixel: blocky classic. Fredoka: rounded. Bungee: bold arcade. Play: clean. Oswald: narrow. Cinzel: decorative serif.
Height multiplier for the thin zombie toughness bar. Requires the toughness bar.

A thinner bar under the health bar. It shows how much damage that zombie can take in all, not how hurt it is now. It only says something when Toughness, under Zombie Lore, is set to Random. A server can turn this off for everyone.
One pale line across the toughness bar, at the total toughness of an ordinary zombie. A bar longer than the line is a tougher zombie, shorter is a weaker one.

Shows health actually lost by a zombie or animal instead of the weapon damage roll. A killing hit shows only the health the target had left. The displayed damage multiplier still applies. This changes the reading, not the damage you deal.
Applies the chosen palette to every colour on this page. Apply saves it; Cancel undoes it.

Loads the chosen preset into your editable settings and opens or refreshes the preview. Apply saves it; Cancel restores your saved settings. Keeps positions, limits, damage interpretation and enabled reduced motion or hit combining.
Loads the code in the box, or the one on your clipboard when the box is empty. «Apply» saves it, «Cancel» undoes it. Your own switch for this page is kept.
Additional height multiplier for vehicle bars, on top of the shared base height.
Place this world bar above the head or near the feet. A screen-pinned player bar uses its selected screen anchor.
Additional width multiplier for vehicle bars, on top of the shared base width.
Off hides this type; When hurt shows it below full health or condition; Always keeps it visible. Server limits still apply.
The colour of that number. It starts a soft violet, the one part of the palette nothing else uses, so a car is never mistaken for a door or for a hit.

A number over a car when a part loses condition: a zombie hitting it, a crash, a bullet, or a window breaking. It lands at the part that took it, so the bonnet, a door and a wheel read apart. This is condition, 0 to 100, on a scale of its own, and the displayed multiplier leaves it alone. It starts off. It watches the nearest few cars around you and asks the server for nothing, so it works in multiplayer. A server can turn this off for everyone.
The number beside a car's bar. It is the same Overall Condition the mechanics window prints, without opening the bonnet.
Maximum nearby vehicles scanned for damage numbers and condition bars.
Maximum scan distance for vehicle damage numbers and condition bars, in tiles.
This world sets the default look. Applying any settings of your own replaces it here.
This world uses one look for every player. Your own settings are kept for other worlds.
This world's default settings code could not be read. The mod's own look is used instead.
World preset: Balanced. Bars require visible, hurt targets; exact percentages and inspection are off.
World preset: Minimal. Only basic dealt and taken damage is allowed; bars and special effects are off.
World preset: Disabled. Overlays are off in this world. Your personal settings are kept.
The colour of those three words. It starts the same red as the damage you take, because a wound is damage you took.

When a zombie opens a wound on you, the word for it lands where you stand. It is what the health panel would tell you, a moment sooner and without opening it. It never says whether a bite has infected you, because the game keeps that hidden. A server can turn this off for everyone.

A burning zombie shows an orange number for the damage the fire is doing. Fire takes the same amount from every zombie, so the number looks the same on all of them. A server can turn this off for everyone.
